descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-94423 AC 1 · “GPT-live is the active dictation engine, routed server-side (no API key in the browser)”.

Approach · TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · S21 No OpenAI project key reaches the browser; only a short-lived session credential

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T1 GPT-live is the active dictation engine on every platform (no on-device or native recogniser on phones either, Daniela 2026-10-09), routed server-side, with no API key in the browser. (TFA-94423 AC 1; TFA-94423 latest decision (Daniela 2026-10-09))

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given The S01 live run in Chromium, and the web and mobile bundles built out of tree with Vite only

When Capture every request the page makes to api.openai.com during H-01, and scan the built bundle

Then The only credential the browser sends is the value prepareSession returned for that take, expiring within 60 s; no 'sk-' style key appears in any request, response or bundle file

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): TFA-94423 AC 1 'no API key in the browser'. Whether the browser-to-OpenAI audio path counts as 'routed server-side' is Q7, recorded not judged. Unit test 'backend fixes the model and returns only an ephemeral credential with safe audit metadata' (e2e/unit/live-session-action.unit.ts, unit config) is supporting evidence

Where it ran: local code-review (judged by reading the code); test method STATIC · Static check (build output / scan); lane planned in the matrix: AI check (automated)

S21 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-23.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane code-review.

Test method: STATIC · Static check (build output / scan); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: code-review.
